correctness.rationale: The fixed-time characteristic function is that of a centered independent Bernoulli triangular array with normalized squared weights one. Finite-head separation and tail cubic bounds prove a Gaussian residual plus a convergent Bernoulli series. Local-time increments have mean (1-theta) s_n h + O(s_n^2) and variance O(s_n^3), giving exact strict-threshold inversion in distribution. Bernoulli third and fourth cumulants show Gaussian iff no nonzero fixed normalized weight survives. Generalized harmonic sum estimates yield each Zipf rate and s=1/2 transition. originality.rationale: The primary July 2026 paper states universal first-order homogeneous-clock quorum behavior but does not report a second-order ranked-weight limit in its accessible introduction and results summary. The new theorem identifies a complete Bernoulli-series/Gaussian profile and sharp Gaussian-versus-nonGaussian Zipf boundary while keeping homogeneous rates. Older Gaussian weighted-empirical-function results have different bounded-weight assumptions. Search results and accessible owned-claim comparisons reveal no direct statement or dominating implication. This remains a best-knowledge assessment with incomplete access to later sections and certain adjacent works.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-threshold quorum-time statistic shares its first-order deterministic limit for every diffuse homogeneous-clock weight vector, yet its uncertainty is not universal. This result classifies the distinct Gaussian and Bernoulli-series fluctuation shapes via ranked weight geometry, identifies an exact power-law transition at exponent 1/2, and derives the harmonic endpoint excess kurtosis -4/5. It is a mathematically motivated complete boundary rather than a contrived finite parameter slice, and does not rely on an unproved downstream application.
